title: The Guardian exists because some Sky actors structurally cannot retain a lawyer at all
content:
A.2.9.1.1.3 defines the Guardian as "a specialized Ecosystem Actor ... exclusively mandated to retain and instruct counsel to assist with the legal defense of actors in the Sky Ecosystem that, due to their organizational structure or circumstances, may be unable to obtain legal representation when pursuing or defending claims against adversarial parties."

The problem it addresses is specific and easy to miss: money is not the only barrier to representation. A law firm needs an identifiable client to sign an engagement letter, run conflict and KYC checks, and take instructions. A pseudonymous delegate, an unincorporated collective, or a DAO with no legal personality can fail every one of those requirements while being perfectly able to pay.

The Guardian resolves this by becoming the client of record — it retains and instructs counsel on the actor's behalf, supplying the legal personality the actor lacks. This is why the Resilience Fund's onchain-only Proof of Eligibility (A.2.9.1.1.1.4.1.1) is coherent: the fund can accept a pseudonymous beneficiary because the Guardian can front the engagement.

Note that the mandate covers "pursuing or defending," so the Guardian is not purely defensive — it can enable an ecosystem actor to bring claims against adversaries, which an unincorporated actor otherwise has no standing mechanism to do. The Guardian is also itself a Resilience Fund beneficiary category (A.2.9.1.1.1.3.3), and the conflict-handling rules treat it as a claim handler parallel to the Technical Committee.
